methods.label: Rewrite every power with base 2
methods.explanation:
Since \(4=2^2\) and \(8=2^3\), rewriting all powers with base \(2\) lets us compare the two sides directly. All bases are positive, so these powers and the usual exponent laws are valid for every real \(x\).

The left side becomes
\[
2^{6x+3}4^{3x+6}
=2^{6x+3}2^{6x+12}
=2^{12x+15}.
\]
The right side becomes
\[
8^{4x+5}=2^{3(4x+5)}=2^{12x+15}.
\]
Thus the two sides are equal for every real \(x\), with no excluded inputs. There are \(\boxed{\text{infinitely many}}\) real solutions, which is greater than \(3\), choice E.
